releases.displayName: Cross-Play Update is Here: Connect with Explorers Everywhere!

items.text: [p align="start"]It’s time to dust off those walkie-talkies because a brand new update has arrived!
[p align="start"]We’re thrilled to announce that cross-play is now available for We Were Here, We Were Here Too, and We Were Here Together!

[p align="start"]That means no matter if you’re playing on PC, PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo Switch, you and your partner can now connect and puzzle your way through Castle Rock together, across all platforms.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33592243/e7f94ee585321594e402fc550ed1e39d16285973.png"]

[p align="start"]This has been one of our most requested features, and we’ve poured extra time and care into patching up the games so that your connection works seamlessly between devices. Whether you’re shouting directions from your desk or puzzling from the couch, your partner is now just one connection away.
[p align="start"]Alongside this update, We Were Here Together has now joined the series on Nintendo Switch, opening the doors for a whole new wave of puzzlers to step into the cold. ❄️
[p align="start"]So find your partner, start the call, and see how far your communication can take you.
Because no matter the platform… The only way out is together.

releases.displayName: Old version available for players with issues

items.text: Our latest maintenance patch was a well over-due patch that upgraded our outdated code, engine, plug-ins, internal systems and more, which is necessary as preparation for the crossplay update that will be released with the Switch releases later this year.

With this, we've seen that the requirements to smoothly run the game have also shifted and lower-end systems that were able to run the game before, could now experience more issues with the game. Since our older games did not save player save files in the cloud, but instead saved these locally, this migration did not go smoothly for everyone. We've seen that our code was not able to detect the save files successfully for everyone, resulting into some players losing their saves.
Most players will have to re-select their checkpoint file by clicking on "change" in the menu, followed by "start new journey" to then select your checkpoint.
For players who are unable to select their checkpoint or are unable to smoothly play the game due to performance or connection issues, we have added an old version of the game before the patch.
Right click We Were Here Together in your Steam library
Go to Properties
Click on Betas
In the drop down menu, select Legacy - PATCH #1.7.6
Maintenance patch upgrading our engine, plug-ins, render pipeline, and internal systems in preparation for the crossplay update that will be released with the Switch releases.
This patch updated our main menu and checkpoints need to be re-selected by clicking "change" and "start new journey".

releases.displayName: New update released! Coming in loud and clear!

items.text: “Loud and clear! Over!” As you may have noticed, we have updated We Were Here Together right here on Steam! This patch implements a new voice-over system called Vivox. This should improve communication between explorers using their walkie-talkies, especially those trapped in Castle Rock and the outskirts of the Antarctic.

You also might see that when booting up We Were Here Together, the main menu has received a bit of a facelift! Not only is it looking better, it will also keep you up to date with what’s going on with the We Were Here Series.

notes.title: Get in touch with other explorers

items.text: Have your joined the official We Were Here Discord server yet? You should!

Not only are there a lot of fellow explorers looking for help or that have rumors about that pesky Jester guy, there is a ton of great creative work being shared on there as well! Take this artwork from one of the alchemy ingredients for example made by ‘CamelotJager’, so cute!

The explorers are always in the mood to celebrate something when they are not trapped in an ice cave or creepy castle halls. You might already have noticed some treats scattered around the basecamp ingame. These are treats related to the Dutch tradition known as ‘Sinterklaas’. Have you found everything yet?

Make sure you do, because those won’t be sticking around forever! In fact, on December 19th, you might want to explore the basecamp even further with your partner. Because there is that one door that wo-ho-ho-on’t open…

Geoff was already featured in an interesting blog post on Agora.io last week, which we'd recommend taking a look at if you're interested in games dev. This week you can get more insights into the We Were Here series and more as Geoff will be taking part in an Airmeet event organized by Agora.io, happening today! What can you expect exactly? We're glad you asked!

Two industry leaders in social gaming, Geoff van den Ouden, Producer of Total Mayhem Games, and Selcuk Atli, CEO of Bunch, will share their insights on how to make games more engaging through social connection, and why you should ditch Discord and add live voice and video directly inside your game
There will also be a Q/A session and a social networking time towards the end, as well as some tips and tricks to increase a game's user base and session times!
If that sounds good to you, check out the event here!

It's update time again! We have tweaks for visual issues, collision, and some performance issues, not to mention some more fixes for walkie-talkie issues. We are particularly interested to hear if the issue with picking up microphones correctly is fixed. Future updates will see continued work on performance as well alongside more general bug squashing.
